title: Committee rejects request to trim police budget
subtitle: Consent agenda approved; levy pressures, regional budget increase and police reporting also discussed before the final meeting of the year.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee met for its last meeting of 2024. The main business was a notice of motion from Councillor R. Deutschmann asking the Waterloo Regional Police Services Board to look again at its 2025 operating budget estimate and cut the net levy impact by $4 million. The committee defeated it {{vote:m3}}.

An amendment from Councillor Wolf would have removed the dollar figures and left the request open-ended. It was also defeated {{vote:m4}}. Supporters said residents want tax relief and that policing is part of one budget. Opponents said the police board had already made reductions and that the larger pressure is on the Regional budget.

The committee also received and approved the consent agenda items {{vote:m2}}. Because this was a committee meeting, nothing here is final. The 2025 budget goes to Regional Council later in December, where the levy increase will be decided. The committee's next meeting is January 14, 2025.

decisions.detail: The committee rejected a request that the Police Services Board further review its 2025 operating budget estimate and cut the net levy impact by $4 million, to no more than $248,468,301 {{vote:m3}}.
The committee rejected an amendment that would have removed the numerical figures and asked the board only to reconsider its estimate {{vote:m4}}.
The committee received the consent agenda items for information and approved them, with no items pulled for separate discussion {{vote:m2}}.

debate: Supporters of the motion said there is one taxpayer and one budget, that other programs face possible cuts, and that residents are asking for relief in every area including policing. They noted the board would not be bound by the request.

Several councillors said the police board had already found savings after repeated reviews. One said these included deferred purchases, reduced reserve contributions and wage gapping, and that further cuts were unnecessary.

Some councillors said the police budget increase is lower than the Regional budget increase, and that the real budget challenge lies in Regional services. One suggested deferring the budget decision to January. Another said earlier opportunities to decide had already been used.

The sponsor of the motion said the committee lacks current staffing information, and argued there was a lack of transparency and oversight. Others disagreed, expressed confidence in the board and staff, and said it was time to move on to the Regional budget.

One councillor proposed removing the numbers to make the request less confrontational and more open. Others said policing is largely a legislated service and that the question is who pays for it, with some hoping for provincial help.
